'''''Phacelia campanularia''''' is a species of [[flowering plant]] in the family [[Hydrophyllaceae]], known by the [[common name]]s '''desertbells''',<ref name=plantsdb>{{Cite PLANTS |id=PHCA3 |taxon=Phacelia campanularia |access-date=31 January 2016}}</ref> '''desert bluebells''',<ref name=ca>[http://www.calflora.org/cgi-bin/species_query.cgi?where-taxon=Phacelia+campanularia ''Phacelia campanularia''.] Calflora.</ref> '''California-bluebell''',<ref name=BSBI07>{{BSBI 2007 |accessdate=2014-10-17 |df=dmy-all}}</ref> '''desert scorpionweed''',<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=NatureServe Explorer 2.0|url=https://explorer.natureserve.org/Taxon/ELEMENT_GLOBAL.2.146581/Phacelia_campanularia|access-date=|website=explorer.natureserve.org}}</ref> and '''desert Canterbury bells'''.<ref name=lj>[http://www.wildflower.org/plants/result.php?id_plant=PHCA3 ''Phacelia campanularia''.] Lady Bird Johnson Wildflower Center. University of Texas at Austin.</ref> Its true native range is within the borders of [[California]],<ref name=ca/><ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 12 January 2018}}</ref><ref name=":0" /> in the [[Mojave Desert|Mojave]] and [[Sonoran Desert]]s, but it is commonly cultivated as an [[ornamental plant]] and it can be found growing elsewhere as an [[introduced species]].<ref name=plantsdb/>

==Description==
This annual herb has an erect stem reaching {{convert|0.7|m|ft}} in maximum height. It is covered in glandular hairs. The leaf blades are somewhat rounded with toothed edges. The [[inflorescence]] is a loose cyme of flowers. The flower has a bright blue corolla up to 4 centimeters long which can be bell-shaped, funnel-shaped, or round and flattened. It can have white spots in the throat. The protruding [[stamen]]s and [[gynoecium|style]] can be 4.5 centimeters long. The fruit is a capsule up to 1.5 centimeters long.<ref name=jeps>[http://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/cgi-bin/get_IJM.pl?tid=37428 ''Phacelia campanularia''.] The Jepson Manual.</ref> It grows in dry, sandy places below {{Convert|4000|feet|meters}}.<ref name="lj" />

==Taxonomy==
Two [[infraspecies]] are usually recognized, called [[subspecies]]<ref name=ca/> or [[variety (botany)|varieties]].<ref name=powo/> 
*''Phacelia campanularia'' var. ''campanularia'' – limited to the Sonoran Desert
*''Phacelia campanularia'' var. ''vasiformis'' – more common, with a wider range, and sometimes with larger flowers
They can intergrade in some areas.<ref name=jeps/>

==Chemistry==
The [[anthocyanin]] pigment phacelianin was isolated from the flowers of this species and is involved in the formation of their blue color. It is also responsible for the blue of the flowers of ''[[Evolvulus pilosus]]''.<ref name=mori>Mori, M., et al. (2006). [https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pubmed/16464482 Structure of anthocyanin from the blue petals of ''Phacelia campanularia'' and its blue flower color development.] ''Phytochemistry'' 67(6), 622-29.</ref>

The juice, sap, or hairs may cause irritation or a skin rash and should be washed from skin as soon as possible.<ref>{{cite web |title=Toxic Plants (by common name) |url=https://ucanr.edu/sites/poisonous_safe_plants/Toxic_Plants_by_common_Name_659/ |website=Safe and Poisonous Garden Plants |publisher=University of California |accessdate=10 November 2020}}</ref>
